title: lint: `required/label` false-positives on list-views (checks top-level view.label; schema only supports list.label)
body:
## Summary

`objectstack lint` rule **`required/label`** false-positives on standard list-views. For every view in a stack it checks `view.label` (top-level), but the supported view schema places the label inside `list.label` / `listViews.*.label` — a **top-level `label` is rejected by the `defineView` types and stripped by the compiler**. So a correctly-authored app reports one `required/label` error per view, and the rule is effectively unsatisfiable.

## Repro

Any app whose views use the canonical `defineView({ list: { label: '…', … } })` shape (incl. `examples/app-crm`). `objectstack lint` →
```
✗ View "?" is missing a label
    required/label  at views[0].label
… (one per view)
```
Adding a top-level `label`/`name` to `defineView({...})` fails `tsc` (`Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'name' does not exist in type …`) and is dropped by `objectstack validate`, so the lint error persists.

## Source

`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` (~L147):
```ts
push(checkLabelExists(view, `${viewPath}.label`, 'View'));
```
`checkLabelExists` tests `item.label`, but a view's display label lives at `view.list.label` (or `view.listViews.<key>.label`).

## Suggested fix

Resolve the view label from where the schema actually stores it, e.g. check `view.label ?? view.list?.label ?? Object.values(view.listViews ?? {})[0]?.label` before flagging `required/label` — or scope the rule to `list`/`listViews` entries.

## Impact

Makes `objectstack lint` unusable as a hard CI gate for any view-bearing app (we had to run it advisory in objectstack-ai/hotcrm). Found during the 7.4→7.7 upgrade (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#365).
